method.summary: The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) stands out among recent advances for its portable in-the-wild data collection capabilities and an integrated policy learning pipeline that enables direct transfer of human demonstrations into deployable robot control policies [ 2 ] . The handheld gripper tool features two compliant parallel fingers actuated by a single spring-loaded trigger, allowing the human demonstrator to control finger position. A camera mounted on each handheld tool provides visual sensing of both the gripper and the external environment. author_stated.limitation: Despite their promise, the developers of UMI acknowledge several factors that may limit the performance and usability of this and similar systems. First, the demonstrations for robot learning are already time-consuming, and handheld gripper tools can make them take even longer. The current learning framework of UMI, for example, requires at least 200 demonstrations to train a single task in a fixed environment. evidence_cards.summary: 论文指出 UMI 示教虽快于遥操作但仍比手工慢、工具重量会造成疲劳并影响 demonstration；实验中改变 UMI gripper fingers 的力分布显著影响打开绷带包装表现，concentrated load grippers 优于 distributed load grippers，作者将其连接到 demonstration quality 和 learned robot control policies。
evidence_cards.source_context: Overall, the usability study demonstrated that altering the force distribution of UMI gripper fingers significantly affected participants’ ability to open bandage packages, with concentrated load grippers outperforming distributed load grippers. These findings highlight that subtle hardware changes can substantially improve demonstration quality and, in turn, the robot control policies learned from them.
